lessons.title: God as Creator, and the Fall of Man - JAMB Self-Tutoring Lesson
lessons.html:
God as Creator, and the Fall of Man

This self-tutoring lesson covers Creation, the Garden of Eden, the Fall, Cain and Abel, and the Tower of Babel. It follows the JAMB CRS topic structure and is designed so a student can study before attempting the 200-question practice bank.

Learning objectives

  • Explain the main ideas without memorising blindly.
  • Correctly identify and define the key terms used in this topic.
  • Relate each term or process to real farm practice.
  • Distinguish closely related terms from one another.

How to study

  1. Read the explanation slowly.
  2. Write out each key term and its definition in your own words.
  3. Cover the definition and try to recall it from the term alone, then reverse it.
  4. Attempt the practice questions.
  5. Read the explanation even when correct.

Worked example method

Read the question carefully, identify the key term or process being asked about, recall its correct definition or example, eliminate options that describe a different (but related) term, then select the option that matches most precisely.

Common mistakes

  • Confusing two closely related terms (e.g. two similar farming or management systems).
  • Choosing an option that is true in general but does not answer the specific question asked.
  • Overlooking key qualifying words such as 'mainly', 'always' or 'not'.
  • Mixing up crop and animal terminology that sound alike.

Self-test checkpoint

Before continuing, explain the topic in your own words and answer one example without looking at the worked method. If you cannot, return to the explanation and try again.

Worked self-tutoring example

Question: What is the meaning of 'Creation' in Christian Religious Studies (JAMB)?

  1. A. the biblical account, found in the book of Genesis, of God bringing the universe and all living things into existence
  2. B. the biblical teaching that God has supreme power and authority over all creation
  3. C. the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which Adam and Eve were commanded not to eat
  4. D. the biblical account of humanity's attempt to build a tower to the heavens, resulting in the confusion of languages

Correct answer: the biblical account, found in the book of Genesis, of God bringing the universe and all living things into existence

Step-by-step explanation: 'Creation' means the biblical account, found in the book of Genesis, of God bringing the universe and all living things into existence.

Exam strategy

JAMB CRS questions mainly test knowledge of biblical events, characters and lessons, not verse memorisation. Build a strong, precise vocabulary for each topic rather than vague general knowledge, since many wrong options are simply the definition of a different (but related) term.

Revision summary

Before moving to the next topic, make sure you can correctly define and give an example for every key term in God as Creator, and the Fall of Man without referring back to this lesson.
